events.title: M7.7 Earthquake Strikes 68km NNW of Ende
events.detail: At 05:58 WITA (21:58 UTC, 14 August) on Saturday 15 August 2026, a shallow magnitude 7.7 earthquake ruptured the Flores Back-Arc Thrust roughly 68 km north-northwest of Ende, East Nusa Tenggara (NTT) province, at a depth of about 10 km. USGS measured it at Mww 7.7; BMKG initially reported magnitude 7.0 before revising upward to 7.7. Germany's GFZ Helmholtz Centre put it at Mw 7.61 at 25 km depth. Shaking was felt across Flores, Lombok, Sumbawa and parts of South and Southeast Sulawesi.

events.title: BMKG Issues Tsunami Warning Within 2 Minutes 16 Seconds
events.detail: BMKG issued a tsunami warning just 2 minutes and 16 seconds after the mainshock, covering East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara, South Sulawesi and Southeast Sulawesi provinces — a response time officials cited as evidence of an improved early-warning system since the catastrophic 1992 Flores tsunami.

events.title: Small Tsunami Waves Recorded at 16 Locations in Four Provinces
events.detail: Localized tsunami waves reached a maximum of 1.61 m at Reok (Manggarai Regency), 0.94 m at Maurole District (Ende Regency), 0.30 m at Labuan Bajo and 0.17 m at Dompu, recorded across roughly 16 coastal monitoring points spanning East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara, South Sulawesi and Southeast Sulawesi — far below the 26-metre run-ups seen in the 1992 Flores tsunami.

events.title: Tsunami Warning Lifted After ~3 Hours
events.detail: BMKG lifted the tsunami warning at approximately 07:30 WIB, roughly three hours after the mainshock, after monitoring detected no further dangerous sea-level rise. The Labuan Bajo Harbormaster (KSOP) reopened sailing the same afternoon.

events.title: Death Toll Climbs From 2 to 47 Within Hours
events.detail: Early reports from CGTN put the confirmed death toll at 2, but the figure climbed rapidly through the day as rescue teams reached collapsed buildings — reaching 14 (Karmactive), then 38 (HNGN/Travelers Today), then 47 (Al Jazeera, ABC News, NBC News) by Saturday evening, illustrating how fast-moving and provisional early casualty counts were.
events.confidenceReason: Casualty figures were revised multiple times within the same day as search-and-rescue teams reached remote areas.

events.title: TNI Deploys 1,267 Personnel; Air Force Flies Aid From Kupang
events.detail: The Indonesian National Armed Forces (TNI) deployed 1,267 personnel to assist emergency operations on Flores. The Indonesian Air Force mobilized three aircraft to ferry aid from El Tari Airport in Kupang to affected areas, while five helicopters, several planes, a naval vessel and search-and-rescue ships were also committed.

events.title: Prabowo Dispatches 50,000 Presidential Aid Packages
events.detail: President Prabowo Subianto ordered 50,000 presidential aid packages of basic necessities — roughly 275 tonnes of supplies — dispatched to East Nusa Tenggara on the day of the quake, ahead of Indonesia's Independence Day.

events.title: 986 Tourists Evacuated From Padar Island
events.detail: 986 tourists stranded on Padar Island inside Komodo National Park were evacuated to Labuan Bajo after the port authority lifted its suspension of maritime transport services following the earthquake and tsunami alert.

events.title: Frans Sales Lega Airport Ceiling Partially Collapses in Ruteng
events.detail: The terminal ceiling at Frans Sales Lega Airport in Ruteng (Manggarai Regency) partially collapsed during the mainshock. Wings Air subsequently cancelled flights through 22 August while safety inspections continued.

events.title: Shaking Unclogs Hydrothermal Vents at Sano Nggoang Crater Lake
events.detail: Seismic shaking from the mainshock unclogged submerged hydrothermal vents beneath Sano Nggoang crater lake in West Manggarai Regency, sending deep magmatic fluids rich in hydrogen sulfide (H2S) and heavy metals to the surface. On contact with oxygen the H2S oxidized into elemental sulfur and sulfuric acid, turning the lake black and driving its pH down to about 3.17 — a well-understood hydrothermal response to seismic activity rather than a new eruption, according to volcanologists, but one posing a localized toxic-gas hazard.
events.confidenceReason: Reported by a single outlet citing geologists; not yet corroborated by BMKG or a volcanological survey statement.

era: Death Toll Climbs, Rescue Operations Expand (16–17 August 2026)

events.title: Toll Reaches 51 as Rescuers Reach Isolated Villages
events.detail: By Sunday 16 August the confirmed death toll rose to 51 as search-and-rescue teams, previously blocked by landslides on the Trans-Flores highway, reached isolated villages in the epicentral zone for the first time.

events.title: Komodo National Park Treks and Snorkeling Resume
events.detail: Treks, viewpoints and snorkeling sites within Komodo National Park resumed operating on 16 August, a day after the tourism ministry confirmed park areas were 'under control'. Other sites — Wae Rebo, Ruteng Pu'u, Kelimutu National Park and the Maumere Bay Islands Marine Nature Park — remained closed.

events.title: M5.7–5.8 Aftershock Kills Two More in Ngada Regency
events.detail: A magnitude 5.7–5.8 aftershock struck Ngada Regency on 17 August, collapsing an already-weakened structure and killing two more people — a reminder that the aftershock sequence carried its own distinct fatality risk separate from the mainshock.

events.title: TNI/Polri Deployment Expands to 3,500 Personnel
events.detail: By 17 August roughly 3,500 members of TNI and Polri (National Police), including about 260 Mobile Brigade Corps personnel, had been dispatched to Manggarai, Maumere and other affected regencies, alongside specialized Basarnas search-and-rescue teams sent from Bali and West Nusa Tenggara.

events.title: Prabowo Leads Independence Day Moment of Silence for Flores Victims
events.detail: During Indonesia's 81st Independence Day ceremony in Jakarta on 17 August, President Prabowo Subianto asked participants to pray for people affected by the disaster in East Nusa Tenggara while leading a nationwide moment of silence, even as the observance continued on schedule.

events.title: Maumere Maritime Terminal Gangway Fails During Evacuation
events.detail: The maritime terminal building in Maumere (Sikka Regency) sustained major structural damage, and a gangway failed during a passenger evacuation, injuring several people trying to flee the port area.

events.title: Ruteng Regional Hospital's Operating Theatre Destroyed
events.detail: Ruteng Regional General Hospital sustained ceiling damage and its operating theatre was destroyed, forcing the evacuation of surgical patients even as the facility remained a treatment hub for quake casualties. Medical specialists were subsequently deployed from Surabaya to reinforce the Ruteng team.

events.title: Death Toll Reaches 54 on Independence Day
events.detail: Indonesia's earthquake death toll reached 54 on 17 August, Indonesia's Independence Day, with thousands still waiting for aid to reach isolated communities as national celebrations continued in Jakarta.

era: Aftershocks Persist, Aid Scales Up (18–19 August 2026)

events.title: Toll Rises to 68 as 12,800 Displaced
events.detail: BNPB spokesman Berton Suar Pelita Panjaitan confirmed the death toll had risen to 68 by Monday 17–18 August, with 12,800 people displaced across Flores, many sheltering in schools, police stations and government-issued tents.

events.title: Toll Reaches 70, Displacement Surges Past 40,000
events.detail: Four days after the mainshock, the confirmed death toll rose to 70 and the number displaced surged to more than 40,000 as damage assessments extended to six regencies, with nearly 12,000 homes damaged.

events.title: Aftershock Count Reaches 2,119, BMKG Warns of Weeks of Shaking
events.detail: By 18 August BMKG had recorded 2,119 aftershocks since the mainshock, ranging from magnitude 1.1 to 6.2, prompting warnings that shaking would continue for weeks and complicating both rescue operations and residents' willingness to return to damaged homes.

events.title: BMKG: Aftershocks Likely to Continue 21–30 More Days
events.detail: As of 05:00 WIB on 19 August, BMKG had logged more than 2,768 aftershocks — 24 of them above magnitude 5.0 and 81 felt by residents — and predicted continued aftershock activity in East Nusa Tenggara for another 21 to 30 days, attributing the sequence to thrust-fault movement on the Flores Back-Arc Thrust.

events.title: NTT Governor Declares 14-Day State of Emergency
events.detail: East Nusa Tenggara Governor Emanuel Melkiades Laka Lena declared a 14-day provincial state of emergency, unlocking emergency budget authority and streamlining coordination of the multi-regency relief effort.

events.title: World Bank Pledges $50 Million in Emergency Funding
events.detail: The World Bank pledged $50 million in emergency recovery funding for Flores, conditional on a full damage assessment being completed by 25 August — one of the largest single international financial commitments announced so far.

events.title: Australia, Singapore Place SAR Teams on Standby; China, Iran Offer Aid
events.detail: Australian and Singaporean search-and-rescue teams were placed on standby, though Jakarta had not formally requested international deployment. China and Iran offered relief and medical assistance, the EU offered Copernicus satellite mapping support, and IFRC began preparing aid for roughly 2,000 people in temporary shelters. Singapore PM Lawrence Wong wrote directly to President Prabowo to convey condolences.

events.title: Power and Telecoms Near Full Restoration After Mass Outages
events.detail: The earthquake knocked out electricity to 566,797 people and disabled 812 cellular sites at its peak. By 19 August, the Ministry of Public Works reported telecommunications were 'nearly all restored' and power restoration was well underway, though remote hamlets remained without service.

events.title: Landslide on Kelimutu Crater Wall Closes National Park
events.detail: A landslide on the crater wall at Kelimutu National Park, famed for its tri-colored volcanic lakes, forced the closure of the site to visitors pending a geological safety assessment.

events.title: Only 32 of 52 Filling Stations Operating Island-Wide
events.detail: Only 32 of Flores' 52 fuel filling stations remained operational, with 20 shut due to power loss, structural damage or safety inspections — a bottleneck slowing relief-vehicle movement and generator refueling across the disaster zone.

events.title: Reports Emerge of Aid Failing to Reach Remote Villages
events.detail: Field reporting documented villages that had received no government assistance two days after the quake. One resident was quoted: 'As for help from the government, there hasn't been any — no tents, no medicine, no food, no drinking water, nothing.' Residents in several areas questioned why public kitchens had not yet been established.
events.confidenceReason: Single-outlet field reporting citing named residents; BNPB has not directly responded to these specific claims of villages receiving zero aid.

events.title: Quake Exposes Widespread Unsafe Housing Construction
events.detail: Analysis following the quake found nearly 80% of Indonesian residential buildings were constructed without engineering oversight or government supervision, and only about 11% of surveyed homes in the affected region met minimum earthquake-resistant standards. NTT's provincial government renovated just 436 homes in 2025 against a stated target of 5,000 for 2026.
events.confidenceReason: Figures drawn from a single advocacy-oriented outlet's analysis; not independently corroborated by official Indonesian housing ministry data in search results.

events.title: Basarnas Budget Cut Draws Criticism Amid Rescue Effort
events.detail: Critics noted that Indonesia's parliament had cut national search-and-rescue agency Basarnas's 2026 budget by 4.5% to Rp1.48 trillion, despite the agency's chief warning capacity needed to improve, not shrink. Basarnas operates only 38 offices across Indonesia's 514 regional jurisdictions. The cut was contrasted with a 30% increase in defense spending to Rp335.3 trillion under President Prabowo.
events.confidenceReason: Budget figures reported by a single politically-oriented outlet; framing of defense-vs-SAR tradeoff is contested by the government.

events.title: Confirmed Toll Reaches 73 Dead, 1,182 Injured
events.detail: As of 19 August, BNPB's confirmed toll stood at 73 dead and 1,182 injured from the mainshock, with two further deaths from the 17 August Ngada aftershock. Local search-and-rescue officials reported no further outstanding reports of people trapped or missing beneath rubble.
events.confidenceReason: Most recent official figure available; BNPB has cautioned totals may still be revised as assessments in remote hamlets continue.

events.title: Jakarta Post Editorial Urges Sustained National Attention
events.detail: In an editorial titled 'Pray for Flores', the Jakarta Post urged the government and public not to let attention fade once the initial rescue phase ended, warning that the harder work of rebuilding homes, schools and hospitals in one of Indonesia's poorer provinces was only beginning.

events.title: Geologists Note Same Fault That Killed 2,500 in 1992
events.detail: Seismologists confirmed the 2026 rupture occurred on the Flores Back-Arc Thrust, less than 40 km from the source of the catastrophic 1992 Flores earthquake and tsunami that killed roughly 2,500 people with run-ups of up to 26 metres. The 1992 event ruptured the thrust's eastern segment; the western segment — including the zone that ruptured in 2026 — has a long history of tsunamigenic quakes dating to at least 1800 (1815, 1857, 1917, 1979, 2018).

events.title: Two Cabinet Ministers Deliver Aid and Condolence Payments in Sikka
events.detail: Coordinating Minister for Food Affairs Zulkifli Hasan and Home Affairs Minister Tito Karnavian visited Sikka Regency on 19 August, distributing thousands of food-aid packages at Laurentius Say Port and Gelora Samadaor Stadium in Maumere and delivering condolence payments to bereaved families. Karnavian instructed local officials not to force residents back into damaged homes while aftershocks continue.

media.caption: Ministers Zulkifli Hasan and Tito Karnavian distribute aid in Sikka Regency

events.title: M5.8 Aftershock Triggers Fatal Heart Attack in Ruteng
events.detail: A magnitude 5.7–6.0 aftershock struck at 06:45 WITA on 20 August, and a resident near Ruteng Regional Hospital died of shock-induced cardiac arrest — the second fatality attributed to the aftershock sequence rather than the mainshock itself, after the 17 August Ngada deaths.

media.caption: Aftermath scene from the Flores earthquake zone, East Nusa Tenggara

events.confidenceReason: Aftershock magnitude reported inconsistently across outlets (5.8 vs 6.0); death itself corroborated by two sources.

events.title: Uncounted Flores Timur Death Surfaces Five Days Later
events.detail: A death that occurred on 15 August in Waiula Village, Wulanggitang District, Flores Timur Regency — a 74-year-old man who fell fatally while fleeing his home during the mainshock — only came to public attention on 20 August. The Flores Timur disaster agency said it had reported 'nil' casualties to the provincial command center, and the case exposed a gap: the regency never declared an emergency-response status, so its data was not being systematically collected alongside the eight regencies that had.

media.caption: Family of Mateus Noba Noba in Waiula Village, Flores Timur Regency

events.confidenceReason: Single regional outlet, but corroborated by direct quotes from the village head and the regency's own disaster response agency.

events.title: Toll Reaches 83 Dead, Displacement Tops 110,000, Aftershocks Pass 4,258
events.detail: As of 21 August 16:00 WIB, BPBD NTT and BNPB reported 83 confirmed deaths (up from 75 the previous day), 986 injured, and 110,785 displaced (up from 92,735 on 20 August). Homes damaged reached 44,946 (17,176 severely, 9,758 moderately, 18,013 slightly), concentrated in Manggarai, East Manggarai and West Manggarai regencies. BMKG recorded 4,258 aftershocks since the mainshock, ranging M1.1–M6.2, with 118 felt by residents. BNPB spokesman Berton Suar Pelita Panjaitan said the newest deaths resulted from indirect impacts of the earthquake rather than building collapse.

media.caption: BPBD NTT casualty and damage tally infographic

events.confidenceReason: Most recent official BNPB/BPBD NTT figure, corroborated by three independent outlets; BNPB has cautioned counts remain provisional.

era: Death Toll Surpasses 100 Amid Delayed Presidential Visit (22–25 August 2026)

events.title: Toll Reaches 91, Aftershocks Pass 5,688
events.detail: BNPB reported the confirmed death toll rose to 91 (up 4 from the previous day) as of Sunday 23 August, broken down as 32 in Manggarai, 31 in East Manggarai, 14 in Nagekeo, 6 in Sikka, 5 in Ngada, 2 in Ende and 1 in West Manggarai. Of the 91 dead, 40 were male, 48 female and 3 still being identified. 1,286 were injured and 161,084 displaced. BMKG's aftershock count passed 5,688 (M1.1–M6.2) by 05:00 WIB the same day.

media.caption: Evacuation efforts in Ronting, Lamba Leda, East Manggarai Regency

events.title: 1,378 Schools Damaged, 177,678 Students Affected
events.detail: BNPB's education-sector damage assessment, 92% complete as of 21 August, found 1,378 schools damaged across Flores, comprising 5,521 damaged classrooms and 502 severely damaged school buildings. The damage affects 177,678 students and 21,166 teachers and education staff. Of the damaged schools, 923 were temporarily closed for safety, 171 switched to remote learning, 35 relocated to emergency facilities, and only 30 continued operating normally pending full assessment of the remainder. Examples cited include 13 classrooms destroyed at SMAK Setia Bakti and the Madrasah Ibtidaiyah Negeri (MIN) 1 Manggarai building in Reo.

media.caption: Madrasah Ibtidaiyah Negeri (MIN) 1 Manggarai building damaged by the earthquake in Reo, Manggarai District

events.title: Toll Reaches 100 Dead; 73,818 Homes and 1,915 Public Facilities Damaged
events.detail: BNPB chief Suharyanto confirmed the death toll reached 100 by Monday 24 August, with 1,603 injured and 180,327 displaced. He said the newest fatalities were earthquake victims who had suffered severe injuries and received hospital care but could not be saved. Homes damaged reached 73,818 (23,276 severely damaged, 17,563 moderately, 32,979 slightly), concentrated in Manggarai and East Manggarai regencies. Damaged public facilities — schools, houses of worship, government offices and other infrastructure — reached 1,915. BMKG recorded 6,409 aftershocks by day 8, 33 above magnitude 5.0 and 139 felt by residents. Suharyanto stressed all figures remain provisional.

media.caption: BNPB casualty update chart for the NTT earthquake

events.confidenceReason: BNPB chief directly quoted; figures explicitly flagged as provisional by the agency itself.

events.title: Key Trans-Flores Routes Reopen; Wolowiro Bridge Recommended for Closure
events.detail: Public Works Minister Dody Hanggodo said several national road sections cut off by earthquake-triggered landslides — Lianunu–Hepang, Krica–Nitung and Krica–Lidi — have been cleared and reopened to aid traffic. The Koro–Maumere section of the vital Ende–Maumere logistics route remains problematic due to continuing active landslides. The Wolowiro (Wolowaru, Ende Regency) bridge sustained severe structural damage; authorities recommended it be closed and a temporary access route built, with one to two more days needed to fully restore several other bridges. This followed an earlier Ministry of Public Works count (23 August) of 34 landslide points and 9 bridges/culverts addressed out of 94 total damaged infrastructure points across 15 national road routes.

media.caption: Road clearance and repair work on a Trans-Flores highway section

events.title: Toll Reaches 103 Dead, 185,131 Displaced, Aftershocks Pass 7,000
events.detail: BNPB spokesman Berton SP Panjaitan confirmed 3 more deaths on 25 August, bringing the confirmed toll to 103 across seven regencies: Manggarai (41), East Manggarai (34), Nagekeo (13), Sikka (6), Ngada (5), Ende (3) and West Manggarai (1). By gender, 55% of victims were women and 45% men; by age, 45% were elderly, 37% adults, 12% children/adolescents and the remainder infants and toddlers. Injured reached 1,666 and displaced climbed to 185,131. BMKG's recorded aftershock count passed 7,029 since the mainshock.

media.caption: RSUD Aeramo (Nagekeo) using tents to treat earthquake patients

events.confidenceReason: Regency breakdown sums exactly to the reported total (103); demographic split corroborated by BNPB spokesman quote.

events.title: Prabowo's Flores Visit Postponed Twice, Still Pending 10 Days On
events.detail: President Prabowo Subianto's planned 22 August visit to inspect earthquake response in Nagekeo Regency was postponed at short notice; NTT Governor Emanuel Melkiades Laka Lena said it was pushed to 'Monday or Tuesday' without giving a reason. Prabowo instead traveled to Kalimantan on 22 August to oversee forest-fire response and attended his presidential chief secretary's wedding in Jakarta on 23 August. State Secretary Minister Prasetyo Hadi said on 23 August the visit was 'being prepared for the near future' but could not confirm a date, adding that the government's early priority was solving problems on the ground rather than a ceremonial visit. As of 25 August — ten days after the quake — no visit had yet taken place.

media.caption: Presidential Palace briefing on the planned NTT earthquake-zone visit

events.confidenceReason: Postponement and rescheduling confirmed by both the NTT governor and the State Secretary's office across multiple outlets; framing of the delay as politically notable reflects sustained local media attention rather than a single outlet's editorializing.

era: Prabowo Finally Visits as Toll Stabilizes at 111 (26–28 August 2026)

events.title: Prabowo Visits Nagekeo Earthquake Zone After Twice-Postponed Trip
events.detail: President Prabowo Subianto arrived by presidential helicopter in Nagekeo Regency on 26 August, eleven days after the mainshock, to inspect the disaster response at a displacement post in Lapangan Berdikari and the Yonif TP 834/WM battalion command post. He was accompanied by State Secretary Minister Prasetyo Hadi, Energy Minister Bahlil Lahadalia and Cabinet Secretary Teddy Indra Wijaya. Prabowo said he had deliberately delayed his visit to give other agencies room to respond first, then distributed Rp200 billion in aid — Rp40 billion to the NTT provincial government and Rp20 billion to each of the eight affected regencies (West Manggarai, Manggarai, East Manggarai, Ende, Ngada, Nagekeo, Sikka and Flores Timur). Officials also disclosed a cumulative aid tally for 15–24 August of 204.22 tonnes of basic foodstuffs, 27.71 tonnes of ready-to-eat meals, 10.29 tonnes of mineral water, plus medicines, tents and two field hospital units that had performed 29 surgical procedures.

media.caption: President Prabowo Subianto arrives in Nagekeo Regency to inspect earthquake response

events.confidenceReason: Visit, attendees and aid figures corroborated by the Presidential Secretariat's own press release and independent outlets; Prabowo's stated reason for the delay is his own account and was not independently verified.

events.title: Toll Reaches 111 as Displacement Falls for First Time Since Quake
events.detail: BNPB reported the confirmed death toll rose to 111 (up 6 — 4 in Manggarai, 2 in East Manggarai) as of Thursday 27 August, with 1,672 injured. Displacement fell to 176,621 — down from 179,037 the previous day and from a peak of 185,131 on 25 August — the first sustained decline since the earthquake, with the steepest drop in Sikka Regency as families began returning home or moving into more permanent shelter. Nagekeo remained the regency with the most displaced residents at 51,284. BMKG's aftershock count reached 8,193 (up from 7,029+ on 25 August), with 146 felt by residents.

media.caption: Damaged Madrasah Ibtidaiyah Negeri school building in Reo, Manggarai District, symbolic of ongoing NTT quake damage

events.confidenceReason: Death toll and injury figures corroborated across CNN Indonesia, Detik and Jatim Times; displacement decline is a new pattern after ten days of continuous rises.

events.title: No New Fatalities Reported on Day 14; Toll Holds at 111
events.detail: BNPB acting data center head Berton Suar Pelita Panjaitan confirmed at an online press conference on Friday 28 August — the earthquake's 14th day (H+14) — that no new deaths had been recorded since the previous day, holding the confirmed toll at 111. Regency breakdown: Manggarai 45, East Manggarai 38, Nagekeo 13, Sikka 6, Ngada 5, Ende 3, West Manggarai 1. By gender, 56.4% of victims were women; by age, 45% were elderly, 37% adults, 12% children/adolescents and 5% toddlers.

media.caption: BNPB spokesman Berton Suar Pelita Panjaitan at the Day 14 online press briefing

events.title: Homes Damaged Revised to 77,912 as BNPB Launches Rehab-Rekon Push
events.detail: BNPB's verified count of damaged homes rose to 77,912 (24,597 severely, 18,537 moderately, 34,778 lightly damaged) as of 27 August, up from 73,818 on 24 August, following by-name-by-address verification across all seven affected regencies. East Manggarai recorded the most severe damage (6,833 homes), followed by Manggarai (6,360) and West Manggarai (3,732). BNPB deployed teams to the seven regencies to accelerate the rehabilitation-reconstruction (rehab-rekon) process, applying 'build back better' standards, though the agency said verification was still ongoing and figures remained provisional.

media.caption: President Prabowo reviews displaced residents in Maumere during the NTT earthquake response

era: Emergency Status Extended to 12 September as Figures Are Revised (29–30 August 2026)

events.title: NTT Extends Earthquake Emergency Status by 14 Days to 12 September
events.detail: East Nusa Tenggara Governor Emanuel Melkiades Laka Lena extended the province's earthquake emergency response status by 14 days, from its original 28 August expiry to 12 September 2026, following a coordination meeting at the BPBD Ende command post on the evening of 27 August. The governor cited BMKG's forecast of continued aftershock activity for another two to three weeks as the main justification; Nagekeo Regency, nearest the epicenter, received an even longer three-month extension. BNPB's Berton Suar Pelita Panjaitan confirmed the 14-day extension the following day, framing it as necessary to keep aid distribution and recovery operations running without an administrative gap.

media.caption: NTT provincial officials announce the 14-day extension of the earthquake emergency response status

events.title: Day 16: Displacement Revised to 188,161, Homes Damaged to 95,567 as Aftershocks Pass 9,765
events.detail: BNPB's 30 August 07:00 WIB update held the confirmed death toll at 111 but revised several other figures: injured fell to 1,631 (223 severe, 1,408 minor) from 1,672; homes damaged rose sharply to 95,567 (46,161 light, 21,992 moderate, 27,414 severe), up from 77,912 on 27 August; and BMKG's aftershock count passed 9,765 (up from 8,193), with 155 felt by residents. Displacement was reported at 188,161 as of the morning count, a net rise from 176,621 on 27 August driven largely by a data-validation correction in Nagekeo Regency that pushed its evacuee count from roughly 3,259 to 21,552 on 29 August; BNPB said the total then fell by 4,142 over the following day as further families returned home, with Manggarai (50,556) and Nagekeo (50,574) now the largest concentrations. BNPB's Berton Suar Pelita Panjaitan said 27,414 families with severely damaged homes urgently need temporary shelter or relocation.

media.caption: Extended emergency response operations continue across NTT's earthquake-affected regencies

events.title: Transport Ministry Begins Staged Repairs of Quake-Damaged Terminals, Airports and Ports
events.detail: Transportation Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said staged repairs had begun on terminals, airports and ports across NTT that sustained earthquake damage, prioritizing facilities with cracks or debris to restore operations quickly. The ministry described the damage as generally minor and said it had not disrupted logistics flows, while promoting sea transport as an alternative route to reach communities cut off by landslide-blocked roads in Flores, leveraging the island's coastal geography to keep aid and essential supplies moving to isolated hamlets.

media.caption: Transportation Minister Dudy Purwagandhi announces staged repairs to quake-damaged transport infrastructure in NTT

era: Aftershocks Pass 10,000, Aid Operations Near Completion (31 August 2026)

events.title: Aftershock Sequence Passes 10,232 Events as Decay Trend Firms Up
events.detail: BMKG recorded 10,232 aftershocks since the 15 August M7.7 mainshock as of 31 August 05:00 WITA, up from 9,765 on 30 August, ranging M1.0 to M6.2 with 35 events at or above M5.0 and 157 felt directly by residents. BMKG said the decay curve is now showing a clearer declining pattern, though continued activity is still expected for another 3-4 weeks.

media.caption: Residents affected by the M7.7 earthquake sheltering near their homes on Palue Island, NTT

events.title: BNPB: 1,954 Tons of Aid Distributed as Air Force Relief Airlift Winds Down
events.detail: BNPB reported 1,954 tons (98.39% of aid received) had been distributed to NTT quake victims by 30-31 August, via TNI AU airlift (565t, plus a further 21t on 30 Aug), the Ready-to-Use Fund (1,065t), sea transport (179t) and overland trucking (145t), reaching distribution hubs in Maumere and Labuan Bajo. Separately, Air First Marshal Ali Gusman said the Air Force's own Halim Perdanakusuma-coordinated relief airlift — 729 tons of food and clothing flown via C-130 Hercules and A400M aircraft to Flores' seven affected regencies — was winding down after a 15-day operation.

media.caption: Food aid handled at a Bulog warehouse for distribution to NTT earthquake-affected residents

events.title: Education Ministry: 1,918 School Units Affected, Only 37 Resumed In-Person Classes
events.detail: Indonesia's Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education (Kemendikdasmen) said its assessment found 1,918 education units affected across seven regencies and 97 sub-districts, including 665 schools severely damaged and roughly 141,207 students with interrupted learning. As of 31 August only 37 schools had resumed in-person emergency learning and 295 had shifted to distance learning. Minister Abdul Mu'ti called recovery a 'shared responsibility' requiring multi-stakeholder collaboration.

media.caption: Residents affected by the M7.7 earthquake sheltering near their homes on Palue Island, NTT

era: Aftershocks Near 11,000 as Recovery Widens (1–2 September 2026)

events.title: Aftershock Count Passes 10,937 as Decay Trend Holds
events.detail: BMKG recorded 10,937 aftershocks since the 15 August M7.7 mainshock as of 1 September 17:00 WIB, ranging M0.9 to M6.2, with 36 events at or above M5.0 and 164 felt directly by residents. A same-day report citing BMKG put the running count at 10,863 as of 12:50 WIB, consistent with continued steady accumulation through the day. The agency reiterated that the aftershock decay curve is trending down, with activity still forecast to taper out toward the end of September, 21-30 days from the mainshock.

media.caption: Displaced Flores earthquake residents still sheltering in tents as the aftershock sequence continues

events.title: Civil Aviation Directorate Expedites Repairs at Five Quake-Damaged NTT Airports
events.detail: Indonesia's Directorate General of Civil Aviation conducted field inspections at five earthquake-damaged airports — Komodo International (Labuan Bajo), Fransiskus Xaverius Seda (Maumere), H. Hasan Aroeboesman (Ende), Soa (Bajawa/Ngada, prioritized) and Frans Sales Lega (Ruteng) — to assess structural damage and speed rehabilitation. Director General Lukman F. Laisa said the ministry is prioritizing repair of building structures and supporting facilities, including passenger terminals and flight-operations facilities, to restore air connectivity across the province.

media.caption: Operations at Komodo Airport, Labuan Bajo, following the Flores earthquake

events.title: Education Ministry Detail: 6,927 Classrooms Severely Damaged, 785 Schools Need Emergency Units
events.detail: A fuller Kemendikdasmen breakdown of the 1,918 affected education units found 6,927 classrooms severely damaged, plus 418 laboratories, 1,928 toilets and 370 teacher residences damaged, and 48,164 members of school communities displaced. 785 schools had requested emergency classroom units (2,908 units needed in total), with only 89 emergency tents installed as of 30 August and 1,221 schools still halted from in-person learning. Minister Abdul Mu'ti called for multi-stakeholder coordination to accelerate the recovery.

media.caption: Education recovery coordination for earthquake-affected NTT schools

events.title: Agriculture Ministry: 1,321.55 Tons of Rice and 7,000 Liters of Cooking Oil Delivered
events.detail: Indonesia's Ministry of Agriculture reported 1,321.55 tons of rice — drawn from the Emergency Food Reserve (881.98t), local government reserves (101.8t) and national food-assistance programs (472.98t) — plus 7,000 liters of cooking oil (100% of target) had been distributed across the seven affected regencies: Ende, Sikka, Manggarai, East Manggarai, Nagekeo, Ngada and West Manggarai. Assessment of cropland damage remains ongoing as officials coordinate to restore agricultural production.

media.caption: Rice aid staged for distribution to Flores earthquake-affected communities
